nodes.title: Quasi-unipotent (σ,∇)-modules and the p-adic local monodromy theorem (statement)
nodes.statement: A (σ,∇)-module M over the Robba ring Γ_an,con is quasi-unipotent if, after tensoring Γ_an,con over Γ_con with a finite extension of Γ_con, M admits a filtration by (σ,∇)-submodules whose successive quotients admit a basis of elements in the kernel of ∇ (when the residue field k is perfect one may require the extension to be residually separable). Theorem 1.1 (local monodromy theorem, proved in the more precise form Theorem 6.12): for any Frobenius σ of Γ_an,con, every (σ,∇)-module over Γ_an,con is quasi-unipotent. Whether a given ∇ admits a compatible Frobenius structure is independent of σ (change-of-Frobenius functors, Tsuzuki).
hypotheses: Γ_an,con is the Robba ring over a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with residue field k (Kedlaya's Chapter 2 notation, not read); σ is any Frobenius lift on it.

The Frobenius structure is essential: the theorem is false for differential modules without Frobenius (the stage's acceptance test), and the conclusion allows a finite extension of the base Γ_con, not only of the coefficient field.
The proof (Theorem 6.12) was not read; only the statement and the deduction strategy of Sections 1.1-1.2 were.
proofSteps: Strategy as stated in Section 1.2: prove a slope filtration theorem for σ-modules over Γ_an,con (Theorem 1.2/6.10) by trivializing σ-modules over large auxiliary rings (Dieudonne-Manin type classification) and descending to the Robba ring; then reduce quasi-unipotence of a (σ,∇)-module to the case of a single slope defined over Γ_con[1/p], where Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem applies.

The independent proofs of Andre and Mebkhout proceed instead through the Christol-Mebkhout weight filtration of the connection; the atlas stage records these as alternative sources requiring separate conventions.
acceptance: Consumers: finite-dimensionality of rigid cohomology with coefficients in an overconvergent F-isocrystal (Crew for curves, Kedlaya math/0208027 in general = RD.5), Kedlaya's p-adic Weil II (RD.6), and Berger's deduction of Fontaine's p-adic monodromy conjecture (de Rham implies potentially semistable) for PadicHodgeTheory R06.3.
A unipotent logarithmic extension has nilpotent residue; the theorem yields a filtration with trivial (horizontal) graded pieces only after the allowed finite extension.

nodes.title: Slope filtration of σ-modules over the Robba ring and reduction of local monodromy to the unit-root case (statements)
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.2 (precise form Theorem 6.10): every σ-module M over Γ_an,con has a canonical filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ ... ⊂ M_l = M by saturated σ-submodules such that each M_i/M_{i-1} is isomorphic over Γ_an,con to a σ-module N_i defined over Γ_con[1/p], the slopes of N_i are all equal to a rational number s_i, and s_1 < ... < s_l. Slopes are defined through the Dieudonne-Manin classification over the maximal unramified extension of the completion of a discrete valuation ring: over R[1/p] every σ-module is a direct sum of standard modules M_{λ,d} (F v_1 = v_2, ..., F v_d = λ v_1) of slope v_p(λ)/d, with the multiset of slopes independent of the decomposition. Reduction: a (σ,∇)-module over Γ_con[1/p] with a single slope is quasi-unipotent by Tsuzuki's unit-root theorem (the essential case being slope 0, where the module becomes a direct sum of trivial (σ,∇)-modules after a finite base extension), so Theorem 1.2 implies Theorem 1.1.
hypotheses: Γ_an,con is not a discrete valuation ring, so slopes cannot be defined directly over it; the filtration theorem is what makes the reduction to Γ_con possible.
Tsuzuki's theorem [T1] on unit-root (σ,∇)-modules is imported, not read; it also specifies the extension needed.
Neither Theorem 6.10 nor 6.12 nor their proofs (Chapters 3-6: auxiliary rings, semiunit decompositions, slope factorizations, descent) were read.
proofSteps: As described in Section 1.4: Chapter 2 recalls the Robba ring, its integral subring Γ_con and the completion (Amice ring); Chapter 3 constructs auxiliary 'big rings' after de Jong; later chapters prove the Dieudonne-Manin type classification over them and descend the filtration.

Deduction of Theorem 1.1 from Theorem 1.2: apply the filtration to the σ-module underlying a (σ,∇)-module, check that the filtration steps are ∇-stable (part of Theorem 6.12, unread), and apply Tsuzuki to each pure-slope quotient after twisting to slope 0.
acceptance: A unit-root F-isocrystal on the annulus becomes trivial after a finite (residually separable, if k perfect) extension; a rank-one module of nonzero slope has a one-step filtration with that slope.
The slopes s_i are rational numbers and the filtration is canonical (functorial), which RD.1's slope-filtration contract must match.
